title: Original LRUCache insertion-occurrence FIFO state
oracle: Source-reviewed literal insertion-order, duplicate-key, missing/nullish and identity expectations; independent external Map plus insertion-occurrence FIFO model for bounded generated set/get histories. Reads never promote keys. Actual returned data objects provide retained Map keys and strict identity, with no private queue/property access or input retention.

trials.execution: Executed partial insertion-occurrence FIFO behavior against actual archived sources at 1051710191 and 1051908825 through the local core Subject: 19 cases, 408 probes per revision, unchanged comparisons; 20 tests passed. A private observer retained all 38 full results before assertions. Explicit diagnostic process mode reports isolated:false; no conventional LRU, TTL, security, container or production scheduling acceptance.
trials.capacityScope: Positive1/2/3/5 plus selected omitted/undefined/zero/negative/NaN/fractional/numeric-string characterization. No original finite capacity domain.
trials.stateScope: set/get only on genuine source constructors. Duplicate insertion queues another key occurrence and can delete a newly overwritten key; no conventional read-recency LRU contract.
trials.identityScope: Real get-returned key/value records are retained. Structurally equal fresh object keys miss; real reference keys and values survive source-defined eviction histories. No input-argument retention, branding or backing alias claim.

exclusions: Despite its module name LRUCache, this source is an insertion-occurrence FIFO cache; no read-recency LRU contract, security property or regression claim.
Only original constructor and public set/get methods. No private Map/queue/field selectors, helpers, callbacks, fake accessor or new runtime authority.
Missing, stored null and stored undefined all return null; get alone does not distinguish membership for these values.
Zero/negative capacity behavior has a nullish dequeued-key guard; no universal occupancy bound is claimed. Coercion, key/value and history domains remain unbounded.
Each case creates a fresh actual instance; no clear/reset/TTL, persisted restart, delivery, provider, original caller, browser/native/network/account or named-library acceptance.
Locally observed diagnostic process execution is not container isolation or production TypeScript scheduling proof.
